knowledge_cards.claim: Gate or expander and multichannel debleeding are distinct operators with different failure modes.
A gate cannot remove coincident bleed while it must remain open for the wanted hit.
Maximum attenuation is an artistic control separable from threshold and timing optimisation.
Gate release and hold must protect wanted decay while respecting nearby bleed events; fixed global milliseconds are unsafe.
Room bleed can provide cohesion and section energy and should be preserved when it serves the arrangement.
Parallel drum spatial layout should normally remain coherent with overhead and source panning unless deliberate displacement passes mono and full-mix tests.
Input-channel permutation training is promising for layout-robust debleeding but unvalidated for multimiked rock drums.
SDR alone is insufficient for accepting debleeding; evaluate attack, decay, cymbal smear, image stability, mono and listener preference.

rule_candidates.name: choose_bleed_operator_explicitly
rule_candidates.when: cross-pickup obscures a drum or destabilises processing
rule_candidates.change: diagnose envelope cleanup, partial expansion, manual editing or joint estimation before choosing operator
rule_candidates.parameter_range_and_origin: no fixed range; operator distinction from source papers
rule_candidates.undo: isolation improves but decay, image or musical glue worsens

rule_candidates.name: partial_range_before_hard_gate
rule_candidates.when: hard gate chatters, sounds abrupt or over-dries the kit
rule_candidates.change: test finite range/floor before full attenuation
rule_candidates.parameter_range_and_origin: -6/-12/-24 dB/hard mute; proposed project experiment grid, not source prescription
rule_candidates.undo: remaining bleed masks target or deeper attenuation causes holes

rule_candidates.name: gate_time_from_decay_and_events
rule_candidates.change: derive timing from wanted transient/decay and next interfering onset
rule_candidates.parameter_range_and_origin: no universal milliseconds; Pro-G 10 ms lookahead is implementation-specific; paper 1 ms/40 ms examples restricted to synthetic kick test
rule_candidates.undo: transient loss, tail truncation, flutter or false trigger

rule_candidates.name: automate_room_by_section_role
rule_candidates.when: static room clutters fills but chorus lacks size
rule_candidates.change: test sectional or hit-level room automation
rule_candidates.parameter_range_and_origin: -3/0/+3 dB project experiment grid; qualitative move from Barresi
rule_candidates.undo: pumping, room discontinuity or masked lead role

rule_candidates.name: parallel_drum_image_coherence
rule_candidates.when: building parallel drum or room return
rule_candidates.change: start with pan relationships matching source and overheads
rule_candidates.undo: image pull, combing, splash or phasey movement

rule_candidates.name: compress_room_for_role_not_level
rule_candidates.when: room should add density or excitement without replacing dry-kit definition
rule_candidates.change: compare no compression, one strong stage and two lighter stages; blend in context
rule_candidates.parameter_range_and_origin: approximately 20:1 is a style-specific video example requiring visual verification; no automatic ratio or GR
rule_candidates.undo: louder-only preference, harsh wash or weakened impact

rule_candidates.name: debleed_metrics_need_perception
rule_candidates.change: combine SDR with transient, spectral, spatial and human ratings
rule_candidates.undo: metric gain lacks consistent listening benefit
